domain: Enterprise Scaling & Framework Transition (SAFe / LeSS / Kanban)
title: Resistance to SAFe ART Launch from Traditional Engineering VPs
context: An enterprise financial institution is launching its first Agile Release Train (ART). A traditional VP of Engineering refuses to allow their component leads to participate in PI Planning, claiming PI Planning is a 'waste of 2 full days of developer output'.
dilemma: How do you gain VP buy-in without sacrificing the core SAFe PI Planning cadence or forcing a compliance-driven mandate?

must_include: Demonstrating cost of delay & dependency risks
Pilot observation option or metrics baseline
common_pitfalls: Escalating directly to CEO without 1-on-1 dialogue

star_model_answer.situation: During an enterprise SAFe transformation at a financial firm, a key Engineering VP refused to send leads to PI Planning.
star_model_answer.task: My task as Lead Agile Coach was to align the VP on the value of PI Planning while securing full team participation.
star_model_answer.action: I scheduled an executive briefing showcasing historical cross-team dependency delays that cost 6 weeks of rework. I reframed PI Planning as a risk-mitigation alignment event, offering to track engineering efficiency metrics post-PI.
star_model_answer.result: The VP agreed to observe Day 1 and participate in draft plan reviews. Post-PI planning, dependency hand-off tickets dropped by 40%, making the VP a vocal sponsor for future ARTs.

title: Choosing Between Pure Scrum, Kanban, and ScrumBan for an Ops/Dev Hybrid Team
context: A software company's Infrastructure & Cloud Engineering team is struggling with Scrum. Interruptions from live production incidents break sprint commitments every single sprint, causing low team morale.
dilemma: The engineering director insists the team stay on 2-week Scrum sprints. How do you coach the leadership and team toward ScrumBan or Kanban?

common_pitfalls: Forcing Scrum on unplanned operational work
Abandoning retrospectives or daily standups completely

star_model_answer.situation: An Infra Ops team was failing 80% of sprint goals due to unplanned production incident spikes.
star_model_answer.task: As Agile Coach, I needed to transition the team to a flow-based ScrumBan model.
star_model_answer.action: I presented historical incident metrics showing 45% of capacity was reactive. I coached the director to adopt ScrumBan: keeping daily standups and retrospectives while introducing explicit WIP limits, an Expedite lane for Sev-1 incidents, and Kanban flow metrics.
star_model_answer.result: Sprint commit-vs-actual friction dropped to zero. Cycle time improved by 35%, and unplanned work was handled systematically.

title: Decoupling Shared Architecture Dependencies across 15 Feature Teams
context: A telecom platform has 15 teams working on a single product backlog. Integration bugs spike at release time because teams modify shared monolithic components independently.
dilemma: How do you coach the engineering organization to adopt LeSS / Nexus integration practices without creating heavy release manager bottlenecks?

must_include: Nexus Integration Team / LeSS Joint Sprint Planning
common_pitfalls: Reverting to traditional change control boards

star_model_answer.situation: 15 feature teams working on a monolithic core suffered 3-week release freeze periods due to integration chaos.
star_model_answer.task: Coach the enterprise towards Large Scale Scrum (LeSS) / Nexus integration governance.
star_model_answer.action: I facilitated the formation of a cross-cutting Integration Guild, introduced automated contract testing in CI/CD, and established Joint Sprint Reviews across feature teams.
star_model_answer.result: Integration defect rates dropped by 65%, and release frequency increased from quarterly to bi-weekly.
